title: Agentic AI in Payments and Financial Transactions: A Survey of Architectures, Safeguards and Open Problems
content: AI agents powered by large language models are beginning to initiate, authorize, and execute financial transactions on behalf of users and institutions. Between 2024 and 2026 the industry shipped the first payment infrastructure purpose-built for this shift: Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), Coinbase's x402, Visa Intelligent Commerce, and Mastercard Agent Pay, while central banks began experimenting with agentic systems inside wholesale payment infrastructures. Yet the academic literature has not synthesized this transition: existing surveys cover LLM agents generally and financial applications of LLMs broadly, but none examine the specific problem of agents that move money. This survey provides a structured review of agentic AI in payments and financial transactions. We analyze 54 primary works spanning agent architectures, production payment protocols, central-bank research, agent identity frameworks, adversarial security literature, and liability scholarship. We propose a four-axis taxonomy (autonomy level, transaction authority, guarantee mechanism, and failure surface) and use it to map every surveyed system. We find that transaction-integrity guarantees such as idempotency, settlement finality, and reconciliation are enforced largely by convention rather than by structure; that machine-verifiable mandates and agent identity remain immature; and that liability allocation for agent-initiated transactions is unresolved across jurisdictions. We conclude with a research agenda covering bounded-autonomy mechanisms, payment-aware agent benchmarks, machine-verifiable mandates, and systemic-risk modelling. A living bibliography accompanies this survey.
